questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: In many developed economies, large and small firms often exist side by side in the same industry. What is most likely to explain the survival of the small firms?

options.A: They each offer a much wider range of products.
options.B: They have a higher minimum efficient scale.
options.C: They pay much higher wages to their staff.
options.D: They provide a more personal level of consumer service.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows short-run (SRAC) and long-run (LRAC) cost curves for a firm. price, cost SRAC SRAC SRAC 3 LRAC O Q output Which statement is correct?

options.A: When each of the three SRAC curves is U-shaped it shows the existence of economies of scale.
options.B: When the LRAC curve is upward-sloping beyond output OQ it shows the existence of diseconomies of scale.
options.C: When the minimum point of SRAC is below that of SRAC it shows the existence of the law

questions.questionText: What is most likely to rise as a firm expands?

options.A: energy costs per unit of output
options.D: the rate of interest paid on borrowing

questions.questionText: In the long run, what is a feature of monopolistic competition, but not of perfect competition?

options.D: the existence of barriers to entry

questions.questionText: A small European airline currently produces at point X on its long-run average cost curve. It wants a bigger share of the European airline market and proposes to merge with another small European airline. The newly merged firm would produce at point Y on the long-run average cost curve, as shown. LRAC costs X Y O output Why might the newly merged firm be able to produce at point Y?

options.A: The new airline can negotiate discounts when buying fuel.
options.B: The new airline has many layers of management.
options.C: The new airline is unable to hire enough pilots.
options.D: The workforce of the new airline lacks morale and is demotivated.

questions.questionText: Some workers in a low-paid job decide to work longer hours to increase their disposable income. However, this decision reduces state-provided benefits, leaving them no better off. What does this describe?
Which policy is likely to be the least effective means of producing a more equal distribution of income amongst households?

options.A: the imposition of minimum wage levels below the levels produced by the market
options.B: the introduction of progressive personal income taxes
options.C: the payment of child benefits to low income households
options.D: the removal of sales taxes on food consumed by lower income households

questions.questionText: The table shows the main characteristics of employment in two occupations. occupation X occupation Y average annual wage $100000 $60000 number of weeks annual leave 5 weeks 10 weeks average length of working week 48 hours 44 hours job security low high length of training course to obtain job qualification 1 year 2 years What can definitely be deduced from the table?

options.A: Those employed in occupation Y attach greater importance to job security.
options.B: Those employed in occupation X attach less importance to leisure activities.
options.C: There will be more competition for places on training courses to enter occupation X than occupation Y.
options.D: Occupation Y has more non-pecuniary advantages than occupation X.

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm that has four possible methods of production to make its desired output. Each method has a different cost and causes a different amount of pollution. The government rules that polluting firms must buy pollution permits that cost $90 each. Each permit allows the firm to emit 1 tonne of pollution. No pollution can be emitted without a permit. Which method of production has least total cost? cost of production pollution caused ($ per day) (tonnes per day)

Economists have proposed that the best policy to promote development is ‘trade not aid’. What is implied by this proposal?

options.B: Developing countries should be given greater access to markets in developed countries.
options.C: Developing countries should use foreign aid to invest in their export industries.
options.D: Developing countries should use trade barriers to promote import substitution.

questions.questionText: What may lead to a reduction in bank lending in a country?

options.A: an increase in commercial banks’ balances with the central bank
options.B: an increase in the liquidity ratios operated by the country’s commercial banks
options.C: an increase in the monetary base of the country
options.D: an increase in the volume of liquid assets held by the country’s commercial banks
